page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The underlying processor is an Intel Xeon 8269CY running at 2.5 GHz with a 35 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB RAM-to-vCPU ratio. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile characterized by a tradeoff between single-core and multi-core execution. Single-core performance is relatively weak, placing in the bottom 25% for stress-ng single-core and the bottom 10% for Geekbench single-core. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression also show poor performance. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, achieve average performance within the middle 50% tier. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate average read and write speeds, though the overall Passmark memory score falls into the bottom 25%.

Given its high memory density of 8.0 GB per core, the ecs.se1ne.4xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require high single-threaded CPU performance. It is well-suited for database operations, Redis caching, and multi-threaded text or image processing, where it delivers average throughput. It can also handle light LLM inference tasks for smaller models, though performance drops significantly on larger models. It is not recommended for compute-intensive, single-threaded applications or workloads requiring high-speed local storage.
